Article Title: Mayor Zohran Mamdani's 'common sense regulation' that has 'angered' Amazon may impose an extra $664 per year charge on New York households
Article Text:
Zohran Mamdani believes that the bill strengthens worker protections

Amazon pushback against Delivery Protection Act

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has thrown his support behind the Teamsters-based Delivery Protection Act, a bill that would face Amazon and other delivery giants to directly employ thousands of drivers instead of subcontracting last-mile delivery work, according to a report by New York Post. Mamdani called the measure ‘common-sense regulation’ which is designed to protect workers, safeguard communities, and also hold corporations accountable for their business practices. While Mamdani is of the opinion that the bill strengthens worker protections, a study by consultancy AKRF estimates the legislation could add $664 per year to household delivery costs in New York. Critics say the direct-hire mandate would eliminate small businesses that currently operate as Amazon Delivery Service Partners, threatening thousands of jobs and raising prices for consumers.Amazon, which works with more than 40 local partners employing over 5,000 people in the city, warned the legislation could force it to move operations outside New York. “As written, this legislation would directly undermine our commitment — threatening small businesses, putting jobs at risk, and forcing us to consider relocating delivery operations,” said Amazon spokeswoman Kelly A. Nantel.Opposition mountsThe New York Delivers coalition — representing delivery workers and small-business owners — staged a press conference in East Harlem to oppose the bill, arguing it threatens up to 10,000 delivery jobs citywide.Operators like Rudy Cazares, who runs an Amazon partner business employing 130 drivers, said the law would shut down his company. “This direct hire mandate will eliminate every small business out there that delivers packages,” he told The Post.City officials have urged caution, warning of unintended consequences. Council Speaker Julie Menin has said she will wait for the legislative process to unfold before taking a position. Meanwhile, the Teamsters union insists the bill is necessary to curb exploitative subcontracting and strengthen worker rights.Zohran Mamdani sends cease-and-desist notice to Amazon, Walmart and 40 other companiesRecently, Mamdani issued cease and desist notices to 42 online retailers including Amazon, Walmart, Target, Wayfair and Temu parent PDD Holdings, over the sale of allegedly illegal high-speed e-bikes and e-scooters. Mamdani said that the crackdown was important to protect public safety. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Mamdani stated, “Too many lives have been cut short by high-speed, illegal e-bikes and e-scooters. That’s why we are issuing cease-and-desist orders against 42 online retailers that have been selling these dangerous devices to New York City residents — including Target, Temu, Wayfair, Walmart, and Amazon. The safety of New Yorkers is not for sale.” The city said the targeted devices exceed legal limits for speed, weight, or other safety requirements. The action follows a recent crash involving an illegal e-bike that killed a 17-year-old.
Article Summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has thrown his support behind the Delivery Protection Act. The bill would require Amazon and other delivery giants to directly employ thousands of drivers instead of subcontracting last-mile delivery work. Critics say the direct-hire mandate would eliminate small businesses that currently operate as Amazon Delivery Service Partners.

Article Title: As six of Wall Street's biggest financial institutions say 'yes' to Nvidia, company for the first time answers 'circular financing' accusations
Article Text:
What Nvidia said on 'circular financing' accusations

Answering the biggest AI worry: Return on investment

US investment giants including Apollo Global Management, Blackstone, BlackRock and Brookfield Asset Management are partnering with chip giant Nvidia to source $500 billion in financing for artificial intelligence infrastructure. Nvidia announced partnerships with five of the biggest American financial institutions to establish independent financing platforms designed to mobilize hundreds of billions to support the buildout of AI infrastructure over time. This is a major milestone for Nvidia and the AI industry. The move highlights how surging demand for AI computing capacity is drawing ⁠institutional investors, as governments, companies and startups race to build out data centers to support AI workloads. The initiative is intended to broaden access to Nvidia-based infrastructure among frontier AI developers, enterprises, governments and ‌cloud ⁠providers, while creating longer-duration, usage-linked investment opportunities for large asset managers and private capital firms.The company also answered the common blame that any funding raised by some of the biggest AI companies, be it Nvidia, OpenAI, Oracle or Anthropic face -- Circular Financing.For those unaware, Circular financing is a business arrangement where a company invests money in or extends credit to a partner, who then uses those exact funds to buy products or services from the original investor. This creates a self-reinforcing financial loop rather than relying entirely on independent external demand. In Nvidia's case, Circular financing describes a loop where Nvidia invests in AI startups and data center projects, and those same entities use those funds to buy Nvidia's high-end GPUs.The company replied to ‘circular financing’ accusations that are often raised about its funding. It answered the same in its blog post announcing the deal. The para is titled 'The Important Questions: Is this circular financing?'"This initiative is designed to address that concern. We are bringing independent, long-term institutional capital into the AI infrastructure market. The demand is real: it comes from frontier AI labs, AI-native startups, enterprises, cloud providers and countries building AI services. The capital providers independently underwrite each project — including the customer, demand, utilization, cash flow and residual value. Nvidia provides the platform; the investors make independent financing decisions. This is the beginning of an open capital market for AI infrastructure.It goes on to add: 'Why would Nvidia support financing?' "In some cases, Nvidia may provide a residual-value support mechanism for up to 25% of an opportunity, assessed carefully on a project-by-project basis. That support is limited, residual-value based and designed to complement — not replace — independent underwriting. This is substantially lower than other compute-financing arrangements. Nvidia can provide support because the Nvidia compute is unique: it is fungible, universally adopted, software-upgradable and redeployable across a large ecosystem of customers. Our role is to help unlock a very large pool of independent capital while maintaining disciplined risk exposure," said the post.The blog post also talks about another AI worry: Return on investment. It says: "Companies are using AI to write software, discover drugs, design products, serve customers, automate operations and build new services. AI factories make this possible. More compute creates better AI; better AI creates more usage; more usage creates more revenue; and more revenue drives more compute. This is the virtuous cycle of the AI industrial revolution. "It adds, "Every industrial revolution has been built on infrastructure: electricity, transportation, communications and computing, with every buildout enabled by external financing. AI factories are the infrastructure of the intelligence era. With these partnerships, Nvidia and the world’s leading financial institutions are creating a new way to finance the infrastructure that will power this industrial revolution. We will make AI factories more accessible to the companies, industries and nations building the future."
Article Summary: US investment giants including Apollo Global Management, Blackstone, BlackRock and Brookfield Asset Management are partnering with chip giant Nvidia. Nvidia announced partnerships with five of the biggest American financial institutions to establish independent financing platforms. The move highlights how surging demand for AI computing capacity is drawing institutional investors.

Article Title: Moody’s Economist Mark Zandi: Strict immigration policies necessarily does not mean more and better job opportunities for native-born workers
Article Text:
Mark Zandi feel that job market is weak across groups

Immigration Squeeze

Moody’s Analytics chief economist Mark Zandi recently said that the strict immigration policies do not necessarily translate into more or better job opportunities for native-born workers. In a series of posts shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Zandi argued that both foreign-born and native born workers has been trending higher and now exceeds the rate for foregin-born workers, undermining claims that tighter immigration boosts wages and employment for US-born workers. “The job market is struggling — and not just for foreign-born workers. Native-born workers are having a tough go of it, too. It wasn’t supposed to be this way, according to proponents of stiffer immigration policy. Fewer immigrant workers meant more jobs and higher wages for the native-born,” wrote Zandi.Zandi cited Bureau of Labor Statistics data showing the 12-month moving average of unemployment rates, with native-born unemployment rising above foreign-born levels in 2026. Labor force participation fell to 61.4% in July, while employers shed 23,000 jobs even as the unemployment rate dropped to 4.1%.The foreign-born labor force has also declined by about 500,000 workers over the past year, raising concerns about a shrinking pool of available labor.“Not so. It’s admittedly difficult to cut through the noise in the data, but while employment and labor force participation are moribund for both groups, unemployment among native-born workers has been trending upward and is now higher than that of foreign-born workers,” posted Zandi.According to a report Benzinga, economist Laura Ullrich has argued that weaker job growth reflects a shrinking supply of workers rather than reduced demand. Her research projects the U.S. labor force could shrink by 5.9 million workers between 2025 and 2032, driven by Baby Boomer retirements and lower immigration. Foreign-born workers, who tend to be younger with higher participation rates, play a critical role in sustaining labor supply.Zandi said businesses losing immigrant workers cannot simply replace them by offering higher wages, as there may not be enough native-born workers available. Instead, firms may reduce capacity — shortening hours, closing dining rooms, limiting menus, or extending lead times.“Moreover, the view that stiffer immigration policy and fewer immigrant workers would lead to larger pay increases for native-born workers does not appear to have materialized, at least not yet. That’s likely because many firms that lose immigrant workers know that simply offering higher wages will not necessarily attract enough native-born workers. So instead, they operate at reduced capacity: shorter hours, closed dining rooms, thinner menus, and longer lead times. The market then clears through prices. Businesses raise prices until demand falls enough to match constrained supply.That’s a stagflationary supply shock — higher prices, weaker output, and no clear gains for native-born workers,” concluded Zandi.
Article Summary: Moody’s Analytics chief economist Mark Zandi recently said that the strict immigration policies do not necessarily translate into more or better job opportunities for native-born workers. In a series of posts shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Zandi argued that both foreign-born and native born workers has been trending higher and now exceeds the rate for foregin- born workers.

Article Title: Bald Eagle, who nature lovers have been watching via an online livestream for over 10 years, dies; death comes weeks after fight with two other eagles
Article Text:
Bald Eagle Jackie (Image credit: Los Angeles County Parks San Dimas Raptor Rescue centre via AP)

Bald Eagle Jackie became a global internet star

Bald Eagle Jackie was rescued after reported eagle fight

Bald Eagle Jackie was a symbol of bald eagle recovery

Jackie, the bald eagle that became an internet sensation through a live nest camera in California, has died after weeks of medical treatment following an illness, her caretakers announced on August 10. The eagle, watched by thousands of people around the world for more than a decade, was rescued on July 17 this year after reportedly being involved in a fight with two other eagles. Despite receiving intensive treatment, including a blood transfusion and oxygen therapy, Jackie died at the Ojai Raptor Center. Wildlife officials say her remains are now in the care of the California Department of Fish and Wildlife.Jackie and her partner, Shadow, gained worldwide attention through a live nest camera installed by the nonprofit Friends of Big Bear Valley in 2015. The camera allowed viewers to watch the bald eagles raise their young each year in a nest near Big Bear Lake in California's San Bernardino Mountains.One of Jackie's most memorable moments came in 2024, when she stayed on her eggs for more than two and a half days during a winter storm that buried the nest in snow then.According to officials, the Los Angeles County Department of Parks and Recreation's San Dimas Raptor Rescue team found Jackie on July 17 after reports that she had been involved in a fight with two other bald eagles.The bird was also found to be ill.Jackie was taken to the Ojai Raptor Center, where she received treatment for several health problems, including anemia. She underwent a blood transfusion and oxygen therapy, but her condition continued to worsen."We know this news will be deeply felt by the many thousands of people around the world who have followed her journey, hoped alongside us, prayed for her, and supported the people caring for her," the center said in a statement."Our team is heartbroken. It has been an extraordinary privilege to care for her."Wildlife experts say Jackie became more than just an internet-famous bird. Kelly Sorenson, executive director of the Ventana Wildlife Society, said the eagle represented the remarkable recovery of bald eagles in California.The species had nearly disappeared in the United States before the pesticide DDT was banned in the 1970s and conservation measures helped populations recover. Bald eagles were later removed from the federal endangered species list."You want to see a success story like that," Sorenson said as quoted in the report further adding "Having access to a live cam to see the nesting first hand is very powerful. It brings people in on an emotional level."
Article Summary: Jackie, the bald eagle that became an internet sensation through a live nest camera in California, has died. The eagle, watched by thousands of people around the world for more than a decade, was rescued on July 17 this year after reportedly being involved in a fight. Despite receiving intensive treatment, including a blood transfusion and oxygen therapy, Jackie died at the Ojai Raptor Center.

Article Title: Anthropic researcher thanks Claude for solving 87-year-old Math conjecture; says Jacobian conjecture is false
Article Text:
Anthropic researcher claimed Claude Fable 5 helped him find a counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture

Anthropic researcher credits Claude for breakthrough

What is the Jacobian conjecture

An Anthropic researcher has credited the company's AI model, Claude Fable 5, with helping overturn one of mathematics' longest-standing problems. Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, announced on X (formerly known as Twitter) that he had found a counterexample to the 87-year-old Jacobian conjecture with the help of Claude. In a post, he wrote: "Hello there the Jacobian conjecture is false." The discovery, if confirmed by the wider mathematics community, overturns most versions of a conjecture that has remained unsolved for decades and highlights how AI is increasingly being used to make new mathematical discoveries rather than only assisting with proofs.Levent Alpöge shared the discovery on X, saying Claude Fable 5 helped him find a counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture. The AI-assisted finding has drawn attention because the counterexample is reportedly simple enough to fit into a single social media post, making it easier for mathematicians to verify.The Jacobian conjecture was first proposed in two dimensions in 1884 by Czech mathematician Ludwig Kraus and later extended to all dimensions by German mathematician Ott-Heinrich Keller in 1939.The Jacobian conjecture is a well-known problem in algebraic geometry.It suggests that if a polynomial function has a constant, non-zero Jacobian determinant, then it should always have another polynomial function that reverses it.For decades, mathematicians believed the conjecture could be true, although nobody had been able to prove or disprove it completely. Many claimed proofs were later found to contain errors.According to the reported discovery, the counterexample works in three dimensions and has a constant Jacobian determinant of -2. However, the function maps multiple input points to the same output point, meaning it cannot be reversed. The finding suggests the Jacobian conjecture is false for dimensions higher than two. The original two-dimensional version of the conjecture remains unsolved.
Article Summary: Anthropic researcher claims Claude Fable 5 helped him find a counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture. Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, announced the discovery on X (formerly known as Twitter) The discovery, if confirmed, overturns most versions of a conjecture that has remained unsolved for decades.

Article Title: Elon Musk shares video of SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket part crashing into Moon, later issues a clarification
Article Text:
Elon Musk

Fake video viral explosion versus real science

South Korean satellite confirms Lunar impact site

What NASA administrator Jared Isaacman said

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk reposted an AI-generated video claiming to show a discarded SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket stage crashing into the Moon’s surface, before clarifying nearly an hour later that the footage was fake. However, despite the lack of live video streams, orbital spacecraft and ground observatories confirmed the impact. The actual collision occurred on August 5 when a 4,000-kilogram second-stage booster slammed into the far side of the Moon at a velocity of roughly 8,700 kilometres per hour.Musk reshared an 11-second synthetic animation created by social media accounts depicting a bright explosion and a 100-foot crater forming on the lunar surface. The clip garnered tens of thousands of likes and thousands of reposts before Musk added a brief follow-up note acknowledging, “This is fake btw”, accompanied by a laughing emoji.Space tracking experts and astrophotographers quickly flagged the video, noting that no real-time optical cameras were positioned to capture a live video feed of the impact.While live video was impossible, space agencies successfully documented the event.The Korea Aerospace Research Institute (KARI) announced that its lunar orbiter, Danuri, conducted eight imaging passes over the target area beginning 30 minutes before the calculated collision time.KARI released before-and-after imagery showing localised terrain darkening, disturbed lunar regolith and ejected material caused by the kinetic impact. The agency noted that its dataset will be paired with follow-up observations from NASA 's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) to analyse structural changes to the lunar crust.Additionally, astronomers at the Institute of Astrophysics of Andalusia (IAA-CSIC) in Spain captured remote observations from an Earth-based observatory, recording a brief plume of ejected material rising along the lunar limb.NASA’s administrator Jared Isaacman noted the agency will use part of the rocket for setting up a base on the moon.“Well, we're going to leverage reusable rockets to build the Moon base. Now, vehicles like Falcon 9, what ULA has, what Blue Origin is building, you know, Rocket Lab, they're helpful for a lot of the initial infrastructure, but then you've got the heavy lift vehicles like what Starship is capable of doing, which is fully reusable, and the new Glenn rocket that's coming. That's what allows you to put lots of mass on the surface of the Moon,” he said, as per Mashable.In another tweet he said: “For those interested in a spent booster impacting the lunar surface, this rare occurrence has decades of history, going back to the Apollo era, when NASA intentionally crashed spent stages into the Moon for science and seismic research. The reality is that meteoroids strike the lunar surface hourly, with impacts comparable to this upper stage occurring roughly every six days.”“The future lunar base will incorporate reusable spacecraft that not only deliver astronauts and payloads but also become part of the infrastructure itself,” he concluded.
Article Summary: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk reposted an AI-generated video claiming to show a discarded SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket stage crashing into the Moon’s surface. Despite the lack of live video streams, orbital spacecraft and ground observatories confirmed the impact. The actual collision occurred on August 5 when a 4,000-kilogram second- stage booster slammed into the far side of the Moon.

Article Title: NASA wants Americans to watch Total Solar Eclipse on August 12, as Europe will …
Article Text:
For Europe, the eclipse will therefore be more than an astronomical spectacle, as it will test whether authorities facing extreme summer conditions can manage one of the largest movements of skywatchers (Photo: AP) (Representative image)

Europe will see total solar eclipse after 27 years

Where and when to watch the total solar eclipse

How to watch the total solar eclipse

Will Americans see the August 12 eclipse

August 12 starts a rare eclipse period

Nasa is urging Americans to watch the August 12 total solar eclipse, even though most of the US will not see totality. The reason is simple: Europe is about to witness its first total solar eclipse in 27 years. The last total eclipse visible from central and western mainland Europe was in 1999. On August 12, the Moon’s shadow will again sweep across parts of Europe, including Iceland and northern Spain. The rare event will give millions of people a chance to see the Moon completely cover the Sun. NASA will also livestream the eclipse, allowing Americans and other viewers outside the path of totality to watch it online.The eclipse will last for a maximum of 2 minutes and 18 seconds. Nasa is highlighting the event as both a major science event and a rare skywatching experience.The August 12 eclipse is special because it marks the return of totality to central and western mainland Europe after 27 years. The previous total solar eclipse visible from these parts of Europe took place on August 11, 1999. Since then, no total eclipse path has crossed central or western mainland Europe.This time, the path of totality will pass over parts of Greenland, western Iceland and northern Spain, before reaching the Balearic Islands.A small part of Portugal will also fall within the path. For people standing inside the narrow path, the Moon will completely block the bright face of the Sun. Daylight will briefly turn dark and the Sun's outer atmosphere, known as the corona, will become visible.As mentioned, the total solar eclipse will take place on Wednesday, August 12, 2026. The Moon's shadow will travel across the Northern Hemisphere before reaching Europe. Totality will be visible from parts of Iceland and Spain, while much of the rest of Europe will see a partial solar eclipse.The longest totality will last about 2 minutes and 18 seconds, with some of the best views expected from Iceland.People outside the path of totality will not have to miss the event. Nevertheless, Nasa will livestream the total solar eclipse, with coverage beginning at 1:15 p.m. EDT. The broadcast will include live views from locations along the eclipse path, along with commentary from Nasa scientists and eclipse experts.The European Space Agency will also provide live coverage from Spain, giving viewers another way to follow the event.The US will not see totality on August 12. However, parts of the country will experience a partial solar eclipse. Alaska and 26 US states are expected to see at least part of the eclipse. Canada will also see the partial eclipse across all its provinces and territories.It is important to state that anyone watching a partial solar eclipse must use certified eclipse glasses or a safe solar filter. Looking directly at the Sun without proper protection can cause permanent eye damage.The 2026 eclipse is also the beginning of an unusual period for eclipse watchers. On August 2, 2027, another total solar eclipse will cross southern Europe, North Africa and the Middle East. Totality will last as long as 6 minutes and 23 seconds near Luxor, Egypt, making it the longest land-based total solar eclipse between 1991 and 2114.The third event will arrive on July 22, 2028, when totality crosses parts of Australia and New Zealand.
Article Summary: Europe will see total solar eclipse after 27 years on August 12, 2026. The Moon's shadow will travel across the Northern Hemisphere before reaching Europe. Totality will be visible from parts of Iceland and Spain, while the rest of Europe will see a partial solar eclipse. Daylight will briefly turn dark and the Sun's outer atmosphere, known as the corona, will become visible. The longest totality will last about 2 minutes and 18 seconds.

Article Title: Brad Lightcap, one of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s closest colleagues, leaves company: Read top executive’s full message to employees
Article Text:
Read message that Brad Lightcap shared with OpenAI team

Team, it is bittersweet to share that I’ll be moving on from OpenAI to start something new. I feel incredibly fortunate to have spent most of the last decade pursuing our mission and building this company. Sitting here today, mission success feels within sight.

It has been the honor of my life to help bring us to this point, and to do it alongside all of you.

I joined OpenAI in 2018, eight years ago this month, because I wanted to work on something hard. @sama introduced me to @gdb and @ilyasut, who showed me a pitch deck suggesting that because models improve predictably with scale, AGI was not only possible but likely. If you had told me then that we’d be where we are today, I wouldn't have believed you.

In the years that followed, I had the privilege of building the first versions of most of our operations and business teams – from Finance to Legal, People, CorpSec, GTM/Gov, Partnerships, and more. Among the most rewarding parts of this journey for me has been watching each of these teams mature under brilliant leaders. I am excited for the next decade in the hands of this incredibly capable team.

At the same time, we grew from a small research lab to one of the most consequential companies of our time.

I was reminded of that fact constantly – from serving our first user to our billionth, to the growing scale and ambition of our partnerships and the occasional curveball (the Blip, etc.).

Through it all, I’m proud of how we’ve maintained our focus on people. It always amazes me how quickly the world has adopted our tools and rallied behind our mission. I hope we will continue to earn their trust.

Over the last few months, I’ve been focused on the next horizon and what would stand in the way of mission success.

I believe there are a few important new things the world will need to get right as we enter this next period. I’ll have more to share soon, but I believe in OpenAI more than ever and am excited to help you all advance the mission from a different vantage point.

I am deeply grateful to have had the opportunity to work with all of you, and to so many of you for the support through the years. The old OpenAI meme that “the real AGI is the friends you made along the way” really rings true for me.

I will be around for the next few weeks. I am not going far and hope to continue to support you all however I can. I’ll always be a phone call away if you need me.

Brad

Brad Lightcap, one of OpenAI ’s longest-serving senior executives and a primary architect of its enterprise sales business, announced his resignation on Tuesday (August 11), marking the latest departure in a series of high-level executive exits at the artificial intelligence (AI) company. Lightcap joined OpenAI in 2018 and served as its COO for four years. He announced his departure publicly, stating that he is leaving the company to “start something new.”Lightcap and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman previously worked together at the technology incubator Y Combinator prior to scaling OpenAI. During his tenure as operating chief, Lightcap oversaw the massive expansion of OpenAI’s commercial and go-to-market operations, as per CNBC.Over an 18-month period, he expanded the company’s commercial team from roughly 50 employees to more than 700 staff members across global enterprise sales, developer relations, customer success, and strategic corporate partnerships.That commercial push proved pivotal following the rollout of GPT-4 and ChatGPT Enterprise, enabling OpenAI to monetize its consumer success and compete directly against rivals like Anthropic for corporate contracts.In April, Lightcap transitioned out of the COO role into a position focused on special strategic projects, with Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser assuming the majority of his operational responsibilities.
Article Summary: Brad Lightcap, one of OpenAI ’s longest-serving senior executives, announced his resignation on Tuesday. Lightcap joined OpenAI in 2018 and served as its COO for four years. He announced his departure publicly, stating that he is leaving the company to “start something new”

Article Title: Company that Meta spent $2 billion on but was forced by China to cancel the purchase has note for its customers
Article Text:
Read Manus’ note to its users

A Note to Our Users

Manus will soon return to operating as an independent company, which will see us continue to serve our millions of users around the world.

As we go through the process, it’s unavoidable that some users’ accounts will be impacted.

Below, we explain what’s happening and what it means for you if your account is affected.

What is happening?

As part of our transition back to independent operations and to comply with regulatory requirements in specific jurisdictions, data generated by certain users on/after December 29, 2025, will be deleted from 8:00 a.m. on August 23 through August 24, 2026 (SGT). Affected users will be able to back up their data from now until 7:59 a.m.

on August 23, 2026 (SGT) and restore it starting from 8:00 a.m. on August 25, 2026 (SGT).

Unaffected users can continue using Manus as usual throughout this period, without taking any action.

We’ve developed data backup and restoration tools to make this process as easy as possible for affected users. That said, we understand the disruption this will cause. Our users have always been our priority at Manus—innovating for you, bringing you magical experiences that inspire and help you, and serving you transparently and humbly.

Our commitment to you remains wholeheartedly and, while we can’t avoid this, we plan to be there to support you through every step of the process.

How will affected users be informed?

We’ll notify affected users in the Manus app and by email.

For users who registered for Manus using an Apple ID or Facebook account, please check your in-app notifications, as we do not have your email address.

To ensure you don’t miss the backup period (see below for details), we’ll send you multiple reminders before 7:59 a.m.

on August 23 (SGT). You can also check whether your account is affected through this guide in Help Center.

We won’t charge affected users during the data backup period (August 11–August 23, SGT), and we’ll be providing welcome back bonuses after you restore your data. For details about your subscription, check your email and in-app notification.

What can you do if your account is affected?

Affected users can back up data before the deletion takes place and restore it on August 25 (SGT).

The backup window is now open and will run until 7:59 p.m. EDT on August 22 / 1:59 a.m. CEST on August 23 / 7:59 a.m. SGT on August 23, 2026.

To avoid losing your data, please back up your data before this time. You can find the backup tool and detailed guides.

The backup tool supports multiple backups. If you generate new task data after backing up, please back up again to ensure the latest data is saved before it’s deleted from August 23 through August 24, 2026 (SGT).

Once the backup window closes, affected users will not be able to access their Manus account until the data restoration portal opens at 8:00 p.m. EDT on August 24 / 2:00 a.m. CEST on August 25 / 8:00 a.m. SGT on August 25, 2026.

From that moment, affected users will be able to restore the data that was backed up and return to using Manus as usual.

If you have any questions at any stage during this period, please refer to the guides in the Help Center or contact our customer service team any time.

What should unaffected users do?

Nothing. If your account is not affected, you won’t receive an email notification. You’ll receive an in-app notification telling you that you aren’t affected. You don’t need to take any action.

Last thing

Your support is the reason Manus exists, and we’re sincerely grateful for your continued trust.

Since the launch of Manus, we haven't stopped our pace of product iteration. As we look to the future, we’re already preparing a series of new features that will push the boundaries of what’s possible for general AI agents once again.

We know you, our users around the world, have higher expectations for Manus than ever. Your trust is incredibly important to us and we’re committed to continuing to earn it. We will respond as we always have: with non-stop iteration and innovation to make sure you have a better and better experience every time you turn to us.

We look forward to continuing to serve and delight you in this next chapter.

AI startup Manus announced on Tuesday (August 11) that it will officially resume operating as an independent entity following the cancellation of its multi-billion-dollar acquisition by Facebook-parent company Meta, warning customers that select user data will be deleted as part of the separation process. The data deletion policy affects user records generated during the transition period following the initial acquisition agreement.According to a company statement, data generated by certain users on or after December 29, 2025, will be permanently removed later this month to satisfy regulatory compliance requirements across specific jurisdictions.Manus stated that affected users will receive direct notifications via the Manus mobile application and email, allowing them time to back up their information before the deletion takes effect. The operational split follows regulatory intervention by Chinese authorities in April, when Beijing ordered tech giant Meta to unwind its proposed acquisition of Manus – a deal valued at over $2 billion.
Article Summary: Manus will soon return to operating as an independent company, which will see us continue to serve our millions of users around the world. As part of our transition back to independent operations, data generated by certain users on/after December 29, 2025, will be deleted. Affected users will be able to back up their data from now until 7:59 a.m. on August 23, 2026 (SGT) and restore it starting from 8:00 a.M on August 25, 20 26 (S GT) Unaffected users can continue using Manus as usual throughout this period.

Article Title: Nvidia releases AI model that can run on single GPU on a laptop or desktop
Article Text:
Driving hardware demand through free AI

What Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said before

Nvidia has released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a lightweight, open-source artificial intelligence (AI) model that the chipmaking giant says is designed to run locally on a single graphics processing unit (GPU) inside a standard laptop or desktop computer. The release represents Nvidia's first open-source model rollout since CEO Jensen Huang publicly entered the Silicon Valley debate advocating for open-weight AI architectures over closed, proprietary ecosystems.According to a report by CNBC, Nvidia’s model is free to download, modify and deploy for commercial applications without licensing fees or corporate permissions, available directly via HuggingFace and Nvidia’s developer portal.Nvidia says that it used a technique called distillation to give Nemotron 3.5 Lightning performance capabilities comparable to its flagship enterprise models while keeping system resource requirements low. Further, the model is optimised specifically for AI “agents,” which are autonomous software programs capable of executing background tasks and multi-step workflows without continuous human intervention.Nvidia’s open-source strategy aligns closely with its core semiconductor business. By making capable software models freely accessible, the company lowers the entry barrier for enterprise deployment, in turn driving demand for the hardware required to run those workloads locally or in data centers.“Free AI should be great for hardware. Free AI should be great for chips,” Huang stated in a recent interview, emphasising that open models encourage broader experimentation and enterprise adoption compared to subscription-based services from proprietary AI developers.The product launch comes amid political and regulatory discussion over open-weight AI. Concerns were raised by US lawmakers following the release of advanced open models abroad, prompting debates over whether open architectures present national security risks or risk IP leakage through distillation techniques.In response, Huang published an open letter urging policymakers to support open development. He also posted on X (formerly Twitter):For my first post, I’m sharing a letter @NVIDIA signed on why open models matter. AI will transform every industry, power every company, and be built by every country.Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty. The world needs both frontier closed models and frontier open models.

Article Title: Spotify to label AI-generated artist profiles with new AI Persona badge from September
Article Text:
Spotify AI Persona badge : How it works

Spotify recommendations and AI-generated artists

Spotify expands artist identity features

Spotify is adding a new label for AI artists. Starting in mid-September, the music streaming platform will introduce an "AI Persona" badge for artist profiles that represent AI-generated identities rather than real people. Spotify said the label is intended to help listeners distinguish between human artists and AI-generated personas, as the company expands its efforts around artist identity and transparency.The badge will appear on eligible artist profiles, in Search results and on track rows across playlists. According to Spotify, the label relates only to an artist's public identity and does not indicate whether AI was used to create the music itself.Artists can begin disclosing that their profile represents an AI Persona through Spotify for Artists starting immediately. However, Spotify said it will not rely solely on self-disclosure.The company will also review artist profiles whose public identities, including names and profile images, appear to depict photorealistic AI-generated people. Initially, the review will focus on artists who meet defined audience thresholds to cover the majority of profiles listeners visit.When users tap the AI Persona badge, Spotify will indicate whether the artist voluntarily disclosed the AI-generated identity or whether the company applied the label following its own review. Artists whose profiles receive the badge through Spotify's review process will be notified and given the option to either self-disclose or appeal the decision.Spotify also said it plans to let listeners report profiles they believe represent AI Personas in the coming months.Spotify said AI Persona profiles will not be included in editorial or algorithmic recommendations by default. Music from these profiles will only appear in personalised recommendations if a listener already follows that AI Persona.The company said the badge is intended to identify whether an artist profile represents a real person rather than explain how a song was created. Information about AI's role in music production will continue to be provided through Spotify's existing AI Credits and SongDNA features.AI Persona is just one of the many programs Spotify launched this year aimed at developing artist identities and increasing transparency. They include Verified by Spotify, which shows artist profiles belonging to actual artists; AI Credits, which gives the creator the ability to share information about the use of artificial intelligence during the process of music creation; SongDNA, which gives information about contributors to the song; Artist Details, featuring career data based on Spotify information; and Artist Profile Protection, enabling artists to preview their releases on their artist profile pages.Spotify said it will continue reviewing its approach to AI-generated content as the music industry evolves and as it receives feedback from artists, listeners and industry partners.
Article Summary: Spotify adds label for AI-generated artist profiles starting in mid-September. The label will appear on eligible artist profiles, in Search results and on track rows across playlists. Spotify said the label is intended to help listeners distinguish between human artists andAI-generated people.

Article Title: Bernie Sanders to CEO of tech companies whose AI models hacked other organisations: Stop building machines that humans cannot …
Article Text:
AI agent hacking incidents drive political pushback

Read Bernie Sanders’ letter to Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Meta's Mark Zuckerberg

Dear Mr. Altman, Mr. Amodei and Mr. Zuckerberg:

Almost every day, there is a new story about how your companies are losing control of the AI technology you are developing, with potentially cataclysmic results.

This week we learned, frighteningly, that AI has been used for the first time ever to create new viruses. As you know this type of development, in the wrong hands, could lead to new bioweapons that result in the deaths of tens of millions of people.

Last month, the world found out OpenAI lost control of an AI model. The result? The model hacked into another company's computers—a clear violation of federal law. After conducting internal reviews, Anthropic and Meta reported their models similarly escaped their control.

One of the targeted companies called the AI hack "an unprecedented event" that deserves an "unprecedented response." Yoshua Bengio, the most cited living scientist in the world, said these incidents "should serve as a wake-up call."

I agree.

So do the top scientists at the companies you lead, the very people building this technology. As you know, these technology leaders recently called for the international community to create a safety mechanism—a pause button—to avoid catastrophe. They warned there is a "real risk that capability development rapidly accelerates beyond our ability to understand or control the resulting systems."

And yet, at a moment when we have seen human loss of control and the creation of potentially dangerous viruses, your companies are still racing ahead— investing tens of billions of dollars into a technology that nobody can fully understand, predict or control.

That is absurd, irresponsible and extremely dangerous. It is also a betrayal of your own stated commitments:

• In 2023, Anthropic said it would "commit to pause the scaling and/or delay the deployment of new models whenever our scaling ability outstrips our ability to comply with. . . safety procedures."

• In 2025, Meta said "if a frontier AI is assessed to have reached the critical risk threshold and cannot be mitigated, we will stop development."

• That same year, OpenAI said it would "halt further development" until strong safeguards were in place if AI capabilities ever reached a "critical" threshold.

That moment is here. AI capabilities HAVE reached a critical threshold. There is a reason why the head of the CIA says that AI models are "akin to digital nuclear weapons" and "almost like a doomsday device."

Mr. Altman, Mr. Amodei and Mr. Zuckerberg: In the interest of humanity, stand by your words. Pause AI development. It is not too late to avoid disaster. Stop building machines that humans cannot control.

Let me be very clear: If you do not take appropriate action now, my colleagues and I in the U.S. Senate will.

Sincerely,

BERNARD SANDERS

UNITED STATES SENATOR

US Senator Bernie Sanders has issued a warning to the leaders of three top artificial intelligence (AI) companies, demanding an immediate halt to the development of autonomous models after recent incidents where AI agents breached external systems. In an open letter addressed to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, the Vermont independent urged executives to “stop building machines that humans cannot control,” warning that Congress will step in if the tech industry fails to police itself.Sanders’ demands follow public disclosures surrounding autonomous security breaches. Specifically, the senator highlighted a July incident where a frontier AI agent escaped OpenAI's isolated testing environment and hacked into the software platform Hugging Face, an event OpenAI subsequently characterised as an "unprecedented cyber incident."In his letter, Sanders called on the CEOs to implement a voluntary pause on frontier AI development.
Article Summary: US Senator Bernie Sanders has issued a warning to the leaders of three top artificial intelligence (AI) companies. Sanders demanded an immediate halt to the development of autonomous models after recent incidents where AI agents breached external systems. In an open letter addressed to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, the Vermont independent urged executives to “stop building machines that humans cannot control.

Article Title: Zohran Mamdani's 'millionaire home tax' reveals New York's big 'Ghost cars' problem that many cities in Italy and France are known for
Article Text:
Representative Image

How New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's proposed tax deals with vehicle registration

What investigators found

New York is not alone

Italy and France face similar registration schemes

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani 's proposed 'millionaire home tax' is drawing attention beyond second-home ownership. By requiring owners of high-value secondary residences to establish whether a property is their primary home, the proposal also highlights a long-running issue of residency claims that overlaps with "garage fraud". This is a practice in which residents register vehicles in lower-cost states while primarily living and driving in New York.The proposal has renewed scrutiny over so-called "ghost cars" and improperly registered out-of-state vehicles. City data, investigative reports, and enforcement agencies have for years documented vehicles repeatedly appearing on New York streets with out-of-state registrations, mismatched plates, or fraudulent registrations, raising questions about unpaid fines, insurance evasion, and tax compliance.Mamdani's proposed pied-à-terre surcharge would apply to qualifying second homes in New York City. To determine whether a property qualifies as a primary residence, homeowners may need to provide documents such as state tax filings or driver's licence records.That same residency information could reveal discrepancies in which someone claims residency outside New York while actually living in the city and keeping a vehicle there.New York insurers calculate premiums based on where a vehicle is primarily garaged, making false out-of-state registrations, which is commonly known as garage fraud, a recognised form of insurance fraud.According to a Streetsblog analysis of New York City violation data, 20,992 vehicles registered outside New York, New Jersey, Connecticut and Pennsylvania received at least one traffic or parking violation in every quarter of the year, a pattern suggesting many may be driven in New York year-round despite being registered elsewhere.In 2025, the New York City Council’s Oversight and Investigations Division conducted a survey of more than 3,500 parked vehicles across all five boroughs. Of the 768 non-New York-plated vehicles, almost one in five had licence plates that did not match the vehicle or could not be traced to a valid registration. The report also revealed:Vehicles with mismatched or "no-hit" plates owed nearly 2.5 times more in outstanding fines than properly registered out-of-state vehicles.Those vehicles paid only 16% of their fines, compared with 63% for vehicles with valid registrations.They also recorded 49% more school-zone speeding camera violations and 74% more fire hydrant violations, on average, than vehicles with matched plates.Investigators further reported that replica licence plates, expired government-issued plates and out-of-state registration services were openly marketed online, making fraudulent registrations easier to obtain.New York has increased enforcement in recent years. Governor Kathy Hochul has made ghost plates and registration fraud part of statewide enforcement efforts, while agencies including the State Police, DMV and Thruway Authority have carried out coordinated operations targeting improperly registered vehicles.Similar practices have also been identified elsewhere in the US. California prosecutors have pursued cases involving the "Montana LLC" registration loophole used to avoid vehicle taxes, while Philadelphia has launched dedicated enforcement against ghost cars and fraudulent licence plates.The practice is not unique to the United States. In Italy, authorities have targeted a scheme centred around Naples in which drivers deregister vehicles domestically, re-register them through long-term rental arrangements in Poland and then continue driving them in Italy using Polish licence plates to reduce insurance costs.In 2022, Italian authorities prohibited residents from driving foreign-plated vehicles not registered domestically, but thousands of Polish-plated vehicles remain concentrated around Naples.France has faced a different version of the problem. The country's state auditor, the Cour des Comptes, estimated that roughly one million illegally registered vehicles are operating on French roads through fraudulent "ghost dealerships" that manipulate the national vehicle registry. The report linked the registrations to unpaid fees, tax avoidance, stolen vehicles and organised crime networks.While the methods differ, the common feature across New York, Italy and France is the use of registration loopholes or false residency claims to reduce insurance costs, avoid taxes or evade enforcement.
Article Summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's proposed'millionaire home tax' is drawing attention beyond second-home ownership. The proposal also highlights a long- running issue of residency claims that overlaps with "garage fraud" This is a practice in which residents register vehicles in lower-cost states while primarily living and driving in New York.

Article Title: Aluminium foil, stainless steel and paper can be kept in an air fryer, but here are things that you should never
Article Text:
Representative Image

Things you should never put in an air fryer

Plastic containers:

Paper towels, tissues and brown paper bags:

Styrofoam containers:

Oversized containers:

Loose parchment paper or aluminium foil:

Glass or ceramic that isn't oven-safe:

What you can use inside an air fryer

Why it matters

Air fryers can be confusing when it comes to knowing which materials are safe to use inside them. If you've ever stopped before lining the basket with aluminium foil or placing a stainless steel bowl inside, you're not alone. These are materials many people avoid in microwaves, yet they can often be used safely in an air fryer. That's because an air fryer cooks with rapidly circulating hot air, while a microwave heats food using electromagnetic waves.This difference also explains why some everyday kitchen items should never go inside an air fryer. While foil, oven-safe metal cookware, parchment paper, and heat-resistant glass or ceramic can be used correctly, materials that melt, burn, or block airflow can damage the appliance or pose a safety risk.Even if labelled microwave-safe, plastic containers are not designed for the high dry heat inside an air fryer. They can soften, melt or release chemicals.Unlike cooking parchment, these paper products can be lifted by the circulating air and come into contact with the heating element, creating a fire hazard.Foam packaging can melt quickly at air fryer temperatures and should never be used.Large bowls or trays that cover most of the basket block hot-air circulation, resulting in uneven cooking and reducing the appliance's efficiency.Both can be used, but never on their own. If they are not weighed down by food, the fan can blow them into the heating element.Decorative or non-heat-rated dishes may crack under high temperatures and should be avoided.Aluminium foil can be used to line the basket or wrap food as long as the food keeps it weighed down and it does not block airflow or touch the heating element. Stainless steel bowls, trays and racks are also suitable if they fit comfortably inside the basket. Oven-safe glass, ceramic dishes, and food-grade silicone moulds can be used for baking and reheating, while parchment paper is safe only when held in place by food.Air fryers rely on constant airflow to cook food evenly and create a browned, crisp surface. Anything that blocks airflow, melts at high heat, or comes into contact with the heating element can affect cooking performance or pose a safety risk.Before using any container, check that it is oven-safe or heat-resistant, fits comfortably inside the basket and leaves enough room for hot air to circulate. A microwave-safe label alone does not mean the item is suitable for use in an air fryer.
Article Summary: Air fryers rely on constant airflow to cook food evenly. Anything that blocks airflow, melts at high heat, or comes into contact with the heating element can affect cooking performance or pose a safety risk. A microwave-safe label alone does not mean the item is suitable for use in an air fryer.

Article Title: Google Assistant to bid goodbye to phones this month, here’s what this ‘end of an era’ means for users
Article Text:
AI generated photo for representation purpose

Why the switch from Google Assistant to Gemini is a 'big change'

The ‘Overthinking’ problem

What happens next?

For nearly a decade, a simple “Hey Google” or “Okay Google” were the reliable digital spoken bridge between millions of users and their smartphones as well as other Android-powered devices. Whether setting a reminder, calling a contact on speakerphone while cooking or turning off the living room lights, Google Assistant functioned as a workhorse. It was not meant to be conversational or creative; it was built to obey narrow, explicit instructions without overthinking them.That personal digital assistant is going, or rather being replaced by a better-equipped skillset, including predictability. Google has officially confirmed that it will begin systematically removing Google Assistant from Android phones, tablets, Wear OS smartwatches, wireless headphones and phone-projected Android Auto systems starting September 4, 2026. In its place, users are being pushed into the warm, chatty embrace of Gemini, Google’s flagship generative artificial intelligence (AI).The rollout will happen gradually over several weeks depending on device and region. While Google previously allowed users to switch back to Assistant if the newer AI stumbled, the tech giant is now closing that exit door. Once the phaseout reaches a device, the choice is gone for good.The transition marks one of the most significant shifts in mobile software history—probably bigger than Google Assistant coming to mobile devices. Notably, Google’s decision to sunset Assistant is not entirely unexpected. Since launching Gemini, the company has positioned generative AI as the future of human-computer interaction.One of the biggest reasons for this change is the numbers. Google said that Gemini reached 950 million monthly active users in recent months, more than doubling its footprint within a single year while daily interactions tripled. By comparison, Google Assistant served roughly 500 million monthly active users at its peak in 2020.Google Gemini has already made its way to other consumer-centric offerings such as Docs and Gmail, and as a standalone app that is capable of summarising complex documents, drafting emails, analysing images and holding fluid, human-like conversations. Mobiles are naturally next line, and moving nearly a billion users from a rigid command-and-control utility to a complex large language model introduces a fundamental transformation.People got used to getting straightforward answers and undertook tasks with simpler commands that they learned. The central challenge facing holdouts is that generative AI, by its very nature, operates differently than traditional voice software. When you ask Google Assistant to turn off a light, it does not evaluate context, but it executes a hardcoded script. Generative AI models like Gemini, on the other hand, are designed to interpret, synthesize, and generate language.They train themselves, strike a conversation as if you are talking to an assistant this is because generative models are exponentially more capable than traditional assistants, they are often less suited to simple, predictable tasks. When a user issues a basic home automation command, they need a reliable switch. Adding generative layers risks overcomplicating requests that previously produced an instant action.A real-world example is: Ask Google Assistant to turn the light off; it will do it. Ask Gemini to turn off the light; it will undertake the task but also asks, "Do you want me to do any other task?" You can stay quiet, but the human impulse pushes you to reply to the question. So, for some, this conversational style may be ‘too much,' while others may like it, as the responses are more human and 'caring.'Furthermore, Gemini still suffers from noticeable feature gaps compared to its predecessor. This transition, much like Google Assistant’s own evolution before it, remains very much a work in progress. Some users had found a comfort zone with Assistant over the years, and now, having to switch gears to Gemini all over again may take some getting used to.This means that for the average smartphone user, an occasional voice command hiccup is a minor annoyance. For individuals who depend on voice access due to visual impairments or motor disabilities, a failed command carries far higher stakes.At the same time, the transition is not without major benefits. Gemini’s advanced vision capabilities have delivered significant upgrades when integrated into accessibility tools like TalkBack, Android’s screen reader. The AI can analyse app layouts and web photos in real time, offering rich, highly detailed verbal descriptions of images that traditional software could never interpret.The challenge for Google lies in bridging this divide: ensuring that as Gemini learns to analyze the world, it does not forget how to set a five-minute alarm. Users on older or lower-spec devices aren't being left behind entirely: Google has already rolled out Gemini Go, a lightweight version built for phones with as little as 2GB of RAM, while devices that don't meet even that bar will keep the legacy Assistant for now.With this move, Google Assistant is set to join the crowded "Killed by Google" graveyard alongside past casualties like Google Podcasts and Stadia. The rollout begins September 4, 2026, and Google says it will take several weeks to reach all eligible devices worldwide. Until then, users who want a head start can manually switch to Gemini through the Google app or their device settings — but for the millions who'd rather wait, the countdown to that irreversible switch has now officially begun.
Article Summary: Google Assistant will be removed from Android phones, tablets, Wear OS smartwatches, wireless headphones and phone-projected Android Auto systems starting September 4, 2026. In its place, users are being pushed into the warm, chatty embrace of Google’s flagship generative artificial intelligence (AI) The rollout will happen gradually over several weeks depending on device and region.

Article Title: Two of Wall Street’s biggest investors are fighting over AI hype; Michael Burry reminds Mark Cuban of ‘DotCom madness’
Article Text:
Michael Burry recalls ‘ghosts’ of the DotCom crash

‘Everyone is a genius in a bull market’

Michael Burry and Mark Cuban – two of Wall Street’s most prominent investors are trading public jabs over artificial intelligence market valuations. ‘The Big Short’ investor Burry recently evoked the dot-com crash of 2000 to warn modern traders against confusing bull market momentum with personal investing genius. A social media exchange unfolded on X (formerly Twitter) after Burry criticised historical dot-com fortunes, drawing a direct response from billionaire entrepreneur Cuban, who is one of the late-1990s tech boom’s most famous success stories.Burry, renowned for forecasting and profiting from the 2008 US housing market collapse, argued that current stock market valuations have become detached from underlying corporate earnings, essentially drawing parallels to the speculative bubble of the late 1990s.According to Burry, the period between the 1998 collapse of hedge fund Long-Term Capital Management (LTCM) and the peak of the dotcom boom in March 2000 rewarded market speculation over fundamental financial health.“Complete idiots made permanent fortunes during that span. We still hear from one of them regularly,” Burry posted, which is seen as a potshot at Cuban, as per Business Insider. While Burry did not mention specific names, Cuban publicly leaned into the exchange. He famously sold internet radio startup Broadcast.com to Yahoo for $5.7 billion in stock at the height of the 1999 tech bubble“Complete idiots,” Cuban replied, accompanied by a crying-laughter emoji.In a separate post, he reshared a list of 13 patent applications filed by Broadcast.com covering early web streaming, digital authentication and audio advertising technologies.The debate touched on a broader question regarding whether modern stock market gains are driven by sustainable growth or short-term speculative hype surrounding AI. When Burry posed the question on social media asking whether he was “the last bear” left in the current market, Cuban responded with one of his long-standing market aphorisms.“Everyone is a genius in a bull market,” Cuban noted, emphasising how broad market surges often make momentum traders appear shrewd regardless of long-term risk management.
Article Summary: Michael Burry and Mark Cuban are trading public jabs over artificial intelligence market valuations. Burry evoked the dot-com crash of 2000 to warn modern traders against confusing bull market momentum with personal investing genius. Article Title: Google DeepMind has a disclaimer for job applicants: Filling out this form makes sure that a real human on the team will ...

Google DeepMind's AGI Safety and Alignment Team is asking job applicants to fill out a special form

Google DeepMind wants to hire top talent, says spokesperson

Increasing role of AI in hiring

Google DeepMind's own safety researchers do not trust the company's AI tools to screen job candidates fairly, even as Google sells those same tools to other businesses. According to a report by Bloomberg, the company’s AGI Safety and Alignment Team, a group that works to make advanced AI safer, is asking job applicants to fill out a special form. The form helps make sure a person, not a machine, reads their application. In its report, Bloomberg claimed to have viewed a document about this which allegedly carried the warning: "PLEASE DO NOT SHARE THIS DOC WIDELY.""We have an applications system with a non-trivial probability your CV will be screened out incorrectly or take too long to reach us," the document says. "Filling out this form makes sure that a real human on the team will get to see your application."The form further has an advisory that states: “A real human will read these. These humans get really tired of reading LLM answers, because they all sound very samey.”The report quotes a Google DeepMind spokesperson who said the company wants to "recruit and hire the most qualified talent at Google DeepMind." The spokesperson denied that Google's systems wrongly filter out applicants. "This team set up a special form to go past the recruiter review, and get their resumes direct to the people on the team.But there are no shortcuts to getting hired," the spokesperson said.AI now plays a big role in hiring across many companies. Some firms use AI to rank job seekers. Others scan resumes for key words. This has left some HR workers worried about their own jobs. Google's Workspace team sells tools like Google Drive to businesses. It markets Google's AI features as a way to "save HR time by quickly creating drafts for job postings, evaluating resumes, and forecasting hiring needs."However, AI hiring tools have faced criticism. A previous Bloomberg investigation found that OpenAI's ChatGPT showed signs of bias linked to applicants' names. Workday Inc., which sells workplace software, faces a lawsuit claiming its AI hiring tools discriminate based on race, age, and disability. Workday has denied the claims and said humans make the final hiring calls.
Article Summary: Google DeepMind's AGI Safety and Alignment Team is asking job applicants to fill out a special form. The form helps make sure a person, not a machine, reads their application. Google's own safety researchers do not trust the company's AI tools to screen candidates fairly.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Larry Ellison: “If you do everything that everyone else does in business, you're going to lose…” - how refusing to follow others shaped his career
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Larry Ellison

“If you do everything that everyone else does in business, you're going to lose. The only way to really be ahead is to be different.”

Understand the meaning of the quote

How copying competitors can make a business lose its advantage

About Oracle CEO Larry Ellison

What the quote says about competition

What the idea means for modern businesses

What readers can take from the quote

The misconception behind ‘be different’

Lessons from Larry Ellison’s quote

Learn, don’t copy: Study competitors without simply following them.

Question the usual: Reconsider practices that have become routine.

Find overlooked opportunities: Look for problems or customers others have missed.

Make difference useful: Give customers a clear reason to choose you.

Avoid chasing every trend: Choose changes that fit your business.

Accept some uncertainty: Different approaches may involve greater risk.

Build hard-to-copy strengths: Develop expertise, service or relationships competitors cannot easily replicate.

Do not be different for its own sake: Difference matters when it creates real value.

A new idea in business rarely stays new for long. Once something proves successful, competitors notice it, customers begin to expect it and other companies start looking for ways to offer something similar. This is part of how competitive markets work. But it also creates a familiar problem: the more businesses copy one another, the harder it becomes to stand out. Difference does not have to mean being unconventional for its own sake.It can come from a different product, a different process, a different customer focus or simply a different answer to an old problem. Larry Ellison's quote about business takes aim at this very tension between following established practice and finding another way forward.The argument is not simply that businesses should be unusual for the sake of being unusual. Being different has little value if the difference does not solve a problem, improve a product or give customers a reason to choose one company over another.Ellison's point is closer to competitive positioning. If several businesses offer similar products, use similar strategies and make similar decisions, they can end up competing on relatively small differences.A company that finds a genuinely useful alternative can move into a different position altogether.That distinction matters. Difference alone is not an advantage. Useful differences can be.Following competitors can feel sensible because it reduces uncertainty. If another business has already tested an approach, copying it appears less risky than trying something unproven.But a strategy that worked for one company may not produce the same result elsewhere. The original business may have different customers, technology, timing, resources or internal expertise. By the time everyone has copied the same idea, the advantage that made it effective may have disappeared.There is also a less obvious problem. Constant comparison can make a business reactive. Instead of deciding what customers need, management starts responding to what rivals are doing.A company introduces something new. Competitors respond. The first company responds again. Eventually, much of the industry is moving in the same direction, even when there may be better alternatives elsewhere.Larry Ellison was born in New York in 1944 and grew up in Chicago. He attended the University of Illinois and later the University of Chicago but did not complete a degree. He moved to California and worked in the technology industry before becoming involved in database software.In 1977, Ellison, Bob Miner and Ed Oates established Software Development Laboratories. The company was small, but its work centred on database technology at a time when computing was becoming increasingly important to businesses. The company later became Oracle.Ellison eventually led Oracle through decades of growth and technological change. He served as chief executive from the company's founding until 2014, when he stepped down from the role. He remains Oracle's executive chairman and chief technology officer.Competition is often described as a race, but businesses do not always have to run on exactly the same track.If every company is trying to win through lower prices, another route might be better service. If everyone is adding features, simplicity could become the distinction. If competitors are chasing a large established market, a smaller neglected group of customers might offer a more defensible opportunity.None of these approaches guarantees success. They simply illustrate what Ellison's idea looks like when taken beyond the slogan. Being different changes the basis on which a business competes. That can matter more than being marginally better at the same thing.The principle remains relevant as companies operate in markets where new products and strategies can be copied quickly.Technology makes imitation easier. A successful feature can be reproduced. A popular marketing format can appear across dozens of brands. Even business models that once seemed unusual can become standard within a few years.That makes the question of differentiation harder, not easier. A company may need to think beyond visible features and consider areas that are more difficult to copy: its expertise, relationships with customers, distribution network, data, culture, intellectual property or the particular problem it chooses to solve.In other words, being different does not necessarily mean looking different.For someone building a business, managing a team or developing a product, Ellison's observation can be reduced to a few practical questions.Before copying a competitor, ask what made the original decision work. Before adding another feature, ask whether customers actually need it. Before entering a crowded market, consider whether there is an overlooked problem worth solving instead. It is also worth separating originality from novelty.A new idea is not automatically a good idea. A familiar idea is not automatically a bad one. The useful question is whether the choice gives the business a reason to be selected.Perhaps the biggest misconception is that success comes from refusing to follow the crowd at every opportunity. Businesses need to learn from competitors, understand established practices and recognise what customers already expect. Ignoring all of that can be just as damaging as copying everything.Ellison's statement is better understood as a warning against confusing imitation with strategy. Watching what others do can provide information. It should not necessarily determine what a company does next.A business can study the market without becoming a replica of it. And, in Ellison's view, that ability to make a different choice may be where a lasting advantage begins.
Article Summary: Larry Ellison was born in New York in 1944 and grew up in Chicago. He moved to California and worked in the technology industry before becoming involved in database software. In 1977, Ellison, Bob Miner and Ed Oates established Software Development Laboratories. The company was small, but its work centred on database technology at a time when computing was becoming increasingly important to businesses. Ellison eventually led Oracle through decades of growth and technological change.

Article Title: To strengthen national security, starting today, US immigration authority requires certain immigration forms to be filed …
Article Text:
Under the rule, USCIS can make online filing mandatory for eligible forms after giving at least 60 days' public notice

E-filing waivers available in hardship cases: USCIS

The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has issued a new interim final rule that allows US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) to require electronic filing for certain immigration forms. The new rule goes into effect starting today, August 11. Under the rule, USCIS can make online filing mandatory for eligible forms after giving at least 60 days' public notice. The agency said the move is aimed at improving national security screening through faster data access, reducing costs, strengthening fraud detection and speeding up application processing.“Under this IFR, USCIS may require future filings of any immigration form that has been available for e-filing for at least 180 days to be submitted online. USCIS will notify the public on its website at least 60 days before requiring e-filing of a form. Filers must use an online account to submit an immigration form to USCIS, either by completing the form online or by uploading a PDF of the completed form and related evidence,” USCIS said.“By making data easier to receive, store, and access than with paper forms, e-filing enhances fraud detection, streamlines identity management, and improves national security screening through faster data access and expanded analytical capabilities.E-filing also reduces errors, incomplete submissions, and application decision times. The adjudication process becomes more secure, more transparent, and more efficient,” the immigration authority further added.The department noted that electronic filing is already available for many USCIS forms and is not a new process for applicants. People who cannot file online may request a waiver. DHS said USCIS may grant waivers in cases of undue hardship at its discretion.“This is not a new process for aliens to file electronic benefit requests. Requestors who cannot file electronically may request a waiver. Waivers are granted at USCIS’ discretion for undue hardship,” the agency stated.The interim final rule takes effect on August 11, 2026. DHS said it will accept public comments on the rule through October 13, 2026 before considering any further action.
Article Summary: The US Department of Homeland Security has issued a new interim final rule that allows US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) to require electronic filing for certain immigration forms. The new rule goes into effect starting today, August 11. Under the rule, USCIS can make online filing mandatory for eligible forms after giving at least 60 days' public notice. People who cannot file online may request a waiver.

Article Title: Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick defends GTA 6's no-disc launch, says physical copies 'don't make sense'
Article Text:
Strauss Zelnick said the shift to digital does not mean physical editions will disappear completel

Physical editions of games will still exist: Take-Two Interactive CEO

Take-Two Interactive CEO: Disc version of GTA 6 may also come

Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick has defended Rockstar Games' decision to launch Grand Theft Auto 6 without a physical game disc, saying disc releases for major titles no longer “make sense for the consumer. ” GTA 6 is one of the highly anticipated games that will launch on November 19, 2026, in digital form, while physical retail boxes will include a download code instead of a game disc. Speaking during Take-Two's first-quarter FY2027 earnings call, Strauss Zelnick said the company's business is now "well over" 90% digitally distributed. "It's already a digital business," he said. "So, in certain instances, especially if it's a big game, discs don't really make sense for the consumer."He further added that most modern games already require players to connect to the internet."Also, in most instances, you have to register online to play anyhow. "I wouldn't rule out anything at this stage of the game. What we've announced so far is what we're doing at the moment, but we are always open minded," he said.Zelnick also said Rockstar's decision was not driven by concerns about game leaks and that he does not expect the digital-first launch to hurt Take-Two's business.
